title: Optimize API for type checking with `ty`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Astral, the team behind Ruff, have created a new type checker called [ty](https://docs.astral.sh/ty/).

I am not completly sure if this is an issue with ty or Streamlit, but currently ty raises an error for `st.stop()` as it does not think the code will never return `st.stop()`. ty is rapidly gaining popularity, so I think it would be good to figure out what goes wrong here. I have tried to troubleshoot it, but I am not familiar enough with the inner workings of Streamlit.


```py
import typing

import streamlit as st

def my_func() -> typing.NoReturn:
    st.write("Hello world")
    st.stop()

my_func()
```

```
error[invalid-return-type]: Function always implicitly returns `None`, which is not assignable to return type `Never`
 --> main.py:5:18
  |
3 | import streamlit as st
4 |
5 | def my_func() -> typing.NoReturn:
  |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
6 |     st.write("Hello world")
7 |     st.stop()
  |
info: Consider changing the return annotation to `-> None` or adding a `return` statement
info: rule `invalid-return-type` is enabled by default
```

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-12442)

I'm leaning a bit more towards that this is caused by a bug in `ty`. `st.stop` is correctly annotated with `NoReturn` and afaik other type checkers are able to treat it that way:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/246a1a087b3302951ab0f69f07112d463315808c/lib/streamlit/commands/execution_control.py#L35

I will relabel it as an enhancement and make it slightly more generic to potentially collect other cases that don't work well with `ty`.
btw. which version of `ty` are you using? We added  `ty` recently to Streamlit itself and - in theory - it should also cover our API typings, but we are still on `0.0.1a16`.

Thank you for the quick response! I will also post this question to [ty](https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/1136).

I am `ty 0.0.1-alpha.20` currently.

This is indeed a limitation of ty at the moment! [USER] responded on the issue over at ty

https://github.com/astral-sh/ty/issues/1136
Closing this since I believe Streamlit is working well together with `ty`.
